What it did not yet have was proof that those elements had compounded into a position comparable to the incumbency Cisco enjoyed in routing or the specialist strength Arista enjoyed in cloud data centres. The competitive position, properly stated, was improving and strategically more coherent. It was not yet settled.

chapters.title: From 2016 Alcatel-Lucent through Lundmark, Infinera, Hotard
chapters.body:
## The Alcatel-Lucent Inheritance

The background catalyst still began with Alcatel-Lucent. Nokia announced the combination in April 2015 and celebrated the first day of combined operations on 14 January 2016. That deal brought the Bell Labs inheritance and the service-provider IP-routing assets without which the later AI-and-cloud pivot would have been much thinner. [Nokia and Alcatel-Lucent to combine](https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2015/04/15/nokia-and-alcatel-lucent-to-combine-to-create-an-innovation-leader-in-next-generation-technology-and-services-for-an-ip-connected-world/) [First day of combined operations](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-celebrates-first-day-of-combined-operations-with-alcatel-lucent/)

## Lundmark's Reset

Pekka Lundmark's 2020-2025 period was the bridge between that inheritance and Hotard's AI framing. The financially relevant summary is that continuing-operations net sales peaked at EUR 23.761 billion in 2022, fell to EUR 19.220 billion in 2024, and recovered modestly to EUR 19.889 billion in 2025. At the same time Nokia launched a 2024-2026 restructuring programme targeting EUR 800 million to EUR 1.2 billion of gross cost-base reduction versus 2023, while continuing to protect R&D. [Nokia in 2024 Annual Report release](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-has-published-its-nokia-in-2024-annual-report-and-filed-its-annual-report-on-form-20-f-for-2024/) [Nokia Q4 2024 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-and-full-year-2024/) [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/)

## Infinera

Nokia announced the Infinera acquisition on 27 June 2024 and closed it on 28 February 2025. The deal was the most important optical-networking event in the company's recent history because it changed scale, customer exposure and manufacturing depth at once. Nokia's own post-close disclosures tied the deal to a 26 per cent pro forma optical market-share position in 2024 excluding China and excluding SLTE and Nokia ASN, plus a EUR 200 million operating-profit-synergy target by 2027. [Nokia to acquire Infinera](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-to-acquire-infinera-to-increase-scale-in-optical-networks-and-accelerate-product-roadmap/) [Nokia Infinera close](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-completes-acquisition-of-infinera-to-create-innovation-powerhouse-in-optical-networks-with-the-scale-to-power-the-data-center-revolution/) [Nokia Q1 2025 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2025-04/nokia_slides_2025_q1_fi.pdf)

## Hotard and the Organisational Turn

Hotard's appointment on 10 February 2025, effective 1 April, was the clearest management catalyst. It was followed by a second wave of leadership changes on 16 June 2025, when Nokia said David Heard would succeed Federico Guillén as President of Network Infrastructure from 1 July 2025, and a third on 19 November 2025, when the company reset the operating model into Network Infrastructure and Mobile Infrastructure from 1 January 2026. [Nokia transition release](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/inside-information-nokia-announces-a-leadership-transition---justin-hotard-appointed-as-successor-to-pekka-lundmark/) [Group leadership changes, June 2025](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-announces-changes-to-group-leadership-team/) [Nokia strategy update](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-announces-new-strategy-evolution-of-its-operating-model-new-long-term-financial-target-strategic-kpis-and-changes-to-its-group-leadership-team/)

## Commercial Proof Points

The commercial catalyst set also became more tangible over the period than the draft reflected. Nokia disclosed IP or AI-infrastructure wins with [Nscale](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-building-ip-network-to-support-ai-workloads-at-nscales-new-sustainable-data-center/), [CoreSite](https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2025/05/13/nokia-selected-by-coresite-for-routing-based-network-edge-solution-to-support-data-intensive-mission-critical-applications/) and [CoreWeave](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-selected-by-coreweave-to-provide-networking-backbone-behind-hyperscale-ai-cloud/), and partnered with [Supermicro](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-and-supermicro-partner-to-deliver-integrated-ai-optimized-data-center-networking-solutions/) around AI-optimised data-centre networking. On the mobile side, it extended or added significant disclosed programmes with [Telefónica Germany](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-and-telefonica-germany-agree-5-year-ran-deal-to-advance-5g-expansion/) and [Virgin Media O2](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-wins-new-5g-ran-deal-with-virgin-media-o2-to-accelerate-its-mobile-transformation-plan/).

## NVIDIA

The cleanest external catalyst was October 2025. Nokia said NVIDIA would make a USD 1.0 billion equity investment through a directed share issue of 166,389,351 new Nokia shares at USD 6.01 per share, alongside a strategic AI-RAN and 6G partnership. By March 2026 Nokia was saying it had 10 publicly committed AI-RAN customers and remained on track to begin customer trials later in 2026. [NVIDIA investment release](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/inside-information-nvidia-to-make-usd-1-billion-equity-investment-in-nokia-in-addition-to-new-strategic-partnership-nokias-board-resolved-on-directed-share-issuance-to-nvidia/) [Nokia AI-RAN update](https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2026/03/01/nokia-accelerates-ai-ran-momentum-with-new-partnerships-driving-path-to-ai-native-6g-mwc26/)

## The Forward Catalysts at the Frozen Date

By 23 May 2026, the catalysts that still mattered were narrower and more operational. They were the pace of Infinera integration, the conversion of AI-and-cloud pipeline into sustained IP and optical revenue, the extent to which the new Mobile Infrastructure segment could improve profitability without sacrificing technology leadership, and whether the NVIDIA partnership produced a real product-and-customer arc rather than a balance-sheet endorsement. Nokia's Q1 2026 slides showed enough progress to keep those questions alive: AI & Cloud net sales up 49 per cent, EUR 1.0 billion of AI & Cloud orders in the quarter, and Network Infrastructure expected to grow 12-14 per cent for full-year 2026. [Nokia Q1 2026 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-04/nokia_slides_2026_q1_fi.pdf)

chapters.title: 5G IP, IP Networks SR Linux, Optical Networks technology, Bell Labs
chapters.body:
## The Alcatel-Lucent Inheritance

Nokia's current technology position in routing, transport and long-horizon research still rested heavily on what it acquired from Alcatel-Lucent and then layered with Infinera. The IP-routing franchise, Bell Labs and the optical base all came through that chain of deals. In the Hotard period, management's task was not to invent those assets but to point them at a more attractive end market. [Nokia and Alcatel-Lucent to combine](https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2015/04/15/nokia-and-alcatel-lucent-to-combine-to-create-an-innovation-leader-in-next-generation-technology-and-services-for-an-ip-connected-world/) [First day of combined operations](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-celebrates-first-day-of-combined-operations-with-alcatel-lucent/)

## SR Linux and the Data-Centre Fabric Push

SR Linux was the software expression of that repurposing. Nokia built it as a cloud-native network operating system for its data-centre and high-performance IP platforms rather than as a re-skinned version of legacy service-provider software. The most important thing by the frozen window was not the product architecture alone; it was the evidence that customers were beginning to buy it for AI-era deployments. Nokia disclosed an IP-network build for [Nscale](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-building-ip-network-to-support-ai-workloads-at-nscales-new-sustainable-data-center/) in December 2024, a routing-based deployment for [CoreSite](https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2025/05/13/nokia-selected-by-coresite-for-routing-based-network-edge-solution-to-support-data-intensive-mission-critical-applications/) in May 2025, and a joint AI-optimised data-centre networking solution with [Supermicro](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-and-supermicro-partner-to-deliver-integrated-ai-optimized-data-center-networking-solutions/) in September 2025.

Nokia's own financial language followed those technical wins. In its Q4 2024 report the company said it had signed important deals with Microsoft and Nscale for data-centre switching products and would invest up to an additional EUR 100 million of annual operating expense to drive EUR 1 billion of incremental data-centre-networking net sales by 2028. By Q1 2026 it was saying AI & Cloud orders had reached EUR 1.0 billion for the quarter. [Nokia Q4 2024 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-and-full-year-2024/) [Nokia Q1 2026 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-04/nokia_slides_2026_q1_fi.pdf)

## 5G Transport Still Mattered

The shift toward data-centre fabrics did not make Nokia's transport role in mobile networks disappear. Its IP and transport products still sat beneath 5G radio and core deployments, which is why many of the largest publicly disclosed mobile contracts retained a transport dimension even when the headline was RAN. Nokia's multi-year [Reliance Jio](https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2022/10/17/nokia-wins-multi-year-deal-with-reliance-jio-india-to-build-one-of-the-largest-5g-networks-in-the-world/) award in India and the 2026 [Virgin Media O2](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-wins-new-5g-ran-deal-with-virgin-media-o2-to-accelerate-its-mobile-transformation-plan/) deal in the UK both sat inside a broader stack in which routing, timing and transport remained essential.

The practical point is that Nokia was trying to sell new AI-data-centre relevance without abandoning the transport logic that had historically tied its IP portfolio to radio accounts. That interdependence was a feature as long as mobile demand remained stable; it was a risk whenever mobile spending retrenched.

## Optical Networks After Infinera

On the optical side, the technology story became more concrete after the Infinera close. Nokia's Q1 2025 slides said the enlarged business would have had 26 per cent pro forma market share in 2024, excluding China and excluding SLTE and Nokia ASN, and reaffirmed the EUR 200 million operating-profit-synergy target by 2027. The commercial follow-through then appeared in growth rates: Optical Networks grew 15 per cent in Q1 2025, 17 per cent in Q4 2025 and 20 per cent in Q1 2026. [Nokia Q1 2025 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2025-04/nokia_slides_2025_q1_fi.pdf) [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/) [Nokia Q1 2026 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-04/nokia_slides_2026_q1_fi.pdf)

Nokia also used the March 2026 OFC window to put more technical detail around that platform. The company announced a suite of application-optimised optical solutions built around four new DSPs and 13 new products, claiming up to 70 per cent total-cost-of-ownership savings in some customer applications. That kind of disclosure was not generic branding; it was product-level signalling that Nokia intended to compete on optical performance as well as portfolio breadth. [Optical solutions launch, March 2026](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-launches-suite-of-applicationoptimized-optical-solutions-for-ai-era-networks/)

## Nokia Bell Labs

Bell Labs remained the most symbolically powerful research asset in the group and, by 2025, one Nokia was again emphasising publicly. Nokia's own centenary release for Bell Labs in February 2025 restated the institution's canonical milestones: the transistor in 1947, Claude Shannon's information theory in 1948 and a century-long record of foundational telecom and computing research. [Bell Labs 100-year release](https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2025/02/06/nokia-bell-labs-celebrates-100-years-of-pioneering-innovations-shaping-the-past-present-and-future/) [Bell Labs history](https://www.nokia.com/bell-labs/about/history/)

What mattered strategically was not nostalgia. Bell Labs remained a brand Nokia could use in standards, recruitment and advanced research partnerships while it repositioned the operating company around AI-native networks, 6G and quantum-safe networking. The research institution did not itself solve the commercial execution question, but it supported Nokia's claim to remain a technology company rather than a pure equipment assembler.

## Patent Portfolio and Technology Standards

The draft's patent section also needed tightening around facts Nokia had actually disclosed. In February 2024 the company said its patent estate had been built on around EUR 150 billion of R&D investment since 2000 and comprised around 20,000 patent families, including more than 6,000 families declared essential to 5G. That disclosure came in the same release that announced the conclusion of the smartphone patent-renewal cycle. [Nokia smartphone renewal cycle](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/inside-information-nokia-concludes-smartphone-patent-license-renewal-cycle/)

By the frozen window, this business was no longer reported as a stand-alone "Nokia Technologies" segment. Following the November 2025 operating-model reset, it became Technology Standards inside Mobile Infrastructure under Patrik Hammarén. The economic significance, however, had not changed: the patent estate remained a cash-generative complement to the more capital-intensive network businesses, and it gave Nokia an upstream position in standards-setting that few equipment peers could match. [Patrik Hammarén appointment](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/patrik-hammaren-appointed-as-president-of-nokia-technologies/) [Nokia strategy update](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-announces-new-strategy-evolution-of-its-operating-model-new-long-term-financial-target-strategic-kpis-and-changes-to-its-group-leadership-team/)

chapters.title: Telecom cycle, Ericsson competition, AI cycle, Huawei dynamics, patent licensing
chapters.body:
## A Cycle That Gave and Then Took Away

The first risk remained the most familiar one: customer spending cycles. On a continuing-operations basis, Nokia's net sales fell from EUR 23.761 billion in 2022 to EUR 19.220 billion in 2024 before recovering only modestly to EUR 19.889 billion in 2025. Nokia's own risk language in the Q4 2025 report still listed changes in customer network investments and the ability of customers to monetise their networks as core group-level exposures. [Nokia in 2024 Annual Report release](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-has-published-its-nokia-in-2024-annual-report-and-filed-its-annual-report-on-form-20-f-for-2024/) [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/)

## Competitive Intensity

Nokia's formal risk disclosures also left no ambiguity about competition. The 2025 report listed "competitive intensity" and the need to keep product roadmaps competitive through additional R&D investment among the principal risks. That language covered different threats in different layers: Ericsson and Samsung in radio, Cisco and Arista in routing and cloud networking, HPE-Juniper in the broader AI-networking stack, and Huawei wherever geopolitics did not narrow the field. [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/)

## The Hyperscaler Bet

The newer risk was execution inside AI and cloud. Nokia had enough evidence by the frozen window to argue that the opportunity was real: AI & Cloud net sales were up 49 per cent in Q1 2026, the company booked EUR 1.0 billion of AI & Cloud orders in the quarter, and it expected Network Infrastructure to grow 12-14 per cent for the full year. But that same disclosure shows why the risk remained material: AI & Cloud still represented only 8 per cent of group sales. The bet was meaningful, not yet dominant. [Nokia Q1 2026 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-04/nokia_slides_2026_q1_fi.pdf)

Integration sat inside that same risk bucket. Nokia's filings repeatedly warned about its ability to execute transactions and realise their expected benefits. Infinera was the obvious current case: Nokia had targeted EUR 200 million of operating-profit synergies by 2027, but the company was simultaneously absorbing the portfolio, raising optical manufacturing capacity and changing internal reporting lines. [Nokia Infinera close](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-completes-acquisition-of-infinera-to-create-innovation-powerhouse-in-optical-networks-with-the-scale-to-power-the-data-center-revolution/) [Nokia Q1 2025 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2025-04/nokia_slides_2025_q1_fi.pdf)

## Supply Chain and Optical Capacity

Nokia's official risk list also singled out component procurement and supply-chain disturbance, including semiconductors. That was not boilerplate. In January 2026 the company said 2026 capital expenditure would rise partly because it was investing in additional manufacturing capacity to support optical-network growth. The supply chain had become part of the strategy. [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/)

The optical layer made this more specific than a generic hardware shortage story. Infinera's last standalone 10-K described its use of indium phosphide-based photonic integrated circuits and in-house manufacturing capabilities as a differentiator. That gave Nokia a stronger proprietary position after the acquisition, but it also meant more operational dependence on ramping specialised optical production successfully. [Infinera 2024 10-K, SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1138639/000113863925000035/infn-20241228.htm)

## Huawei and Policy Risk

Huawei remained the central geopolitical variable. In the UK, the government had placed Huawei's removal from 5G networks on a legal timetable running to the end of 2027. That supported Nokia's position in some western tenders, but it also underscored how much carrier competition could still be shaped by government decisions rather than product alone. [UK government Huawei decision](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/huawei-to-be-removed-from-uk-5g-networks-by-2027) [Huawei legal notices issued](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/huawei-legal-notices-issued)

The risk cut both ways. Where restrictions persisted, Nokia benefited from a narrower vendor field. Where they eased, or where they never existed, Nokia still faced a full-stack Chinese rival with scale across radio, transport and optical. That is why Nokia's public language increasingly combined technical claims with the language of trust, resilience and western-provider status.

## Patent Licensing and Renewal Risk

Nokia Technologies, later Technology Standards, remained a financial stabiliser but not a risk-free one. Nokia concluded its smartphone patent-renewal cycle in February 2024 and said no major smartphone licence agreements were due to expire for a number of years, yet the same release made clear how much the economics still depended on renewals, catch-up payments and enforcement. [Nokia smartphone renewal cycle](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/inside-information-nokia-concludes-smartphone-patent-license-renewal-cycle/)

The 2025 risk factors continued to highlight the timing and value of new, renewed and existing patent-licensing agreements, together with litigation and the regulatory landscape for licensing. That was not theoretical. The annual run-rate might have stabilised around EUR 1.4 billion by late 2025, but the path there had depended on the successful conclusion of a long smartphone renewal cycle. [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/)

## The Leadership and Operating-Model Risk

There was also a management-layer risk unique to the frozen window. Nokia was not only integrating Infinera; it was also replacing the head of Network Infrastructure, moving to a new two-segment reporting structure, and having Hotard run Mobile Infrastructure on an interim basis while a permanent appointment was pending. That sort of organisational fluidity can sharpen accountability. It can also slow execution when the company is simultaneously trying to win new hyperscaler accounts and defend old carrier relationships. [Group leadership changes, June 2025](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-announces-changes-to-group-leadership-team/) [Nokia strategy update](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-announces-new-strategy-evolution-of-its-operating-model-new-long-term-financial-target-strategic-kpis-and-changes-to-its-group-leadership-team/) [Emma Falck appointment](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-appoints-emma-falck-as-president-of-mobile-infrastructure-and-member-of-the-group-leadership-team/)

chapters.title: Hotard era execution, Infinera integration, AI data centre routing
chapters.body:
## The Hotard Inheritance, Updated

By the frozen snapshot date, Hotard was no longer inheriting only a declining post-2022 revenue line. He was running a company that had already posted a modest full-year recovery in 2025, reset its operating model around Network Infrastructure and Mobile Infrastructure, and begun to report measurable AI & Cloud traction. Reported continuing-operations net sales were EUR 19.889 billion in 2025, versus EUR 19.220 billion in 2024, and Q1 2026 brought 4 per cent top-line growth with AI & Cloud net sales up 49 per cent year on year. [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/) [Nokia Q1 2026 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-04/nokia_slides_2026_q1_fi.pdf)

## Infinera and Optical

The Infinera acquisition remained the most immediate operating variable because it was already changing the numbers that mattered most to the growth case. Optical Networks grew 17 per cent in Q4 2025 and 20 per cent in Q1 2026, while management continued to point to EUR 200 million of targeted operating-profit synergies by 2027. Nokia also said 2026 capital expenditure would rise in part to fund additional optical manufacturing capacity. The company was therefore not waiting passively for integration benefits; it was spending to accelerate them. [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/) [Nokia Q1 2026 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-04/nokia_slides_2026_q1_fi.pdf)

## Routing and AI Cloud

The better near-term read-through on the AI data-centre thesis sat in Network Infrastructure rather than at group level. In January 2026 Nokia said Network Infrastructure should grow in line with its long-term 6-8 per cent CAGR target in 2026, with the combined Optical Networks and IP Networks businesses again expected to grow 10-12 per cent. Three months later, Q1 2026 slides tightened that message by saying Network Infrastructure should grow 12-14 per cent for the full year and that AI & Cloud orders had reached EUR 1.0 billion in the quarter. [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/) [Nokia Q1 2026 slides](https://www.nokia.com/system/files/2026-04/nokia_slides_2026_q1_fi.pdf)

## Mobile Infrastructure and Capital Allocation

The other side of the outlook was discipline rather than acceleration. Nokia's 2026 comparable operating-profit guide remained EUR 2.0 billion to EUR 2.5 billion, and management repeatedly described the mobile market as stable rather than booming. The strategic burden therefore remained asymmetric: Mobile Infrastructure had to protect profitability and cash generation while Network Infrastructure tried to earn a larger share of AI-and-cloud spending. [Nokia Q4 2025 report](https://www.nokia.com/newsroom/nokia-corporation-financial-report-for-q4-2025-and-full-year-2025/)

## What Had to Happen Next

The outlook by 23 May 2026 was therefore more concrete, but not yet proven. Nokia had to keep Infinera on schedule, convert AI-and-cloud demand into repeatable routed-plus-optical revenue, preserve the licensing cash flow now housed inside Technology Standards, and avoid letting the still-larger mobile base deteriorate while resources were redirected. The company had finally aligned its structure, leadership language and investment agenda around that task. The unresolved question was whether the income statement would follow quickly enough to validate the story before investors tired of the transition.

Strategic refocus under new CEO Justin Hotard (since April 2025) toward AI data centre infrastructure including IP Networks routing for hyperscaler customers plus Optical Networks (post-Infinera acquisition close February 2025).
structural_observations: Justin Hotard CEO succession April 1 2025 — brought from Intel Data Center and AI Group; strategic posture toward AI data centre infrastructure.
Infinera acquisition (announced June 2024, closed February 28 2025 for ~$2.3B) substantially scaled Optical Networks segment with strong hyperscaler customer relationships.

leadership.key_finding: Nokia Corporation's executive structure reflects the strategic transformation through 2024-2025 from Pekka Lundmark's CEO leadership (August 2020-March 2025) to Justin Hotard's CEO succession (April 2025-present). Hotard joined from Intel Corporation where he had been Executive Vice President and General Manager of the Data Center and AI Group; the strategic mandate has been the AI data centre opportunity development through the Network Infrastructure business group particularly the IP Networks routing portfolio plus the broader operational and strategic posture continuation. The executive team layers the new Hotard strategic leadership with CFO Marco Wirén (since January 2021), the business group leadership across Network Infrastructure (Federico Guillen), Mobile Networks (Tommi Uitto), Cloud and Network Services, and Nokia Technologies (the patent licensing business), and broad operational and technology leadership. The board is chaired by Sari Baldauf (since 2020, the principal long-tenured female CEO/board leadership in Finnish technology industry) and includes long-tenured directors plus recent additions calibrated to the AI data centre infrastructure customer category positioning.

board_of_directors.framing: Öistämö brings deep Nokia industry operating experience including prior senior leadership roles at Nokia in earlier periods. The continuing Nokia-industry-operational perspective complements the broader board governance framework.

leadership.board_composition_observation: Nokia Corporation's board pairs Chair Baldauf (multi-decade Nokia EVP of Networks operating experience) and CEO Hotard with directors who bring relevant operational and industry depth: Brown for broader technology-industry executive experience, Hook for telecommunications-industry CEO perspective (the most directly customer-side relevant single director profile given the broader telecommunications customer base), Kozel for telecommunications-and-technology industry executive experience including the prior Cisco Systems senior leadership, Horan for technology-industry executive experience, Dannenfeldt for finance and accounting audit governance, Werner-Dietz for HR governance, Skou for industrial-industry CEO experience, Öistämö for continuing Nokia operational continuity. The composition reflects the company's multi-business-group positioning across telecommunications, network infrastructure, mobile networks, cloud and network services, and patent licensing categories. The Baldauf Chair role plus the Hook telecommunications-CEO experience plus the Kozel Cisco-Systems-senior-leadership experience are the most strategically calibrated single director choices for the broader telecommunications-customer-category-relevant board governance.
